fixed.q: In HTML body tag, which of the following attribute indicates the colour of the hyperlinks after the mouse is clicked on it?
fixed.w: ALINK sets the colour of an active link (at the moment it is clicked); VLINK sets the colour of visited links.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT an attribute that included by the HR tag which puts a horizontal line on the page?
fixed.w: The <HR> tag has SIZE, WIDTH, ALIGN and NOSHADE attributes; there is no SHADE attribute.

fixed.q: Which of the following tags of HTML is a container for the tags that contain information about the page?
fixed.w: The <head> element is a container for metadata tags such as <title>, <meta>, <link> and <style>.

fixed.q: Which of the following form is correct to show a 'comments' in the HTML language?
fixed.w: An HTML comment is written <!-- comment -->.

fixed.q: Which of the following HTML tags is used to put a line break in the text?
fixed.w: inserts a line break.

fixed.q: Which of the following parameters is used to create a hyperlink in HTML?
fixed.w: The href attribute of <a> creates a hyperlink.

fixed.q: Which of the following target values opens the linked document in the full body of the window?
fixed.w: Target="_top" opens the link in the full body of the window, breaking out of frames.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) Class is one of the HTML global attributes which specifies one or more class names for an element (refers to a class in a style sheet). ii) HTML is a markup language used for server-side processing. iii) CSS describes how HTML elements are to be displayed on screen, paper, or in other media.
fixed.w: Class is a global attribute and CSS controls presentation, but HTML is client-side markup, not server-side processing.

fixed.q: Which attribute in HTML table tag defines the number of columns in a column group?
fixed.w: The span attribute of <colgroup>/<col> sets how many columns the group spans.

fixed.q: How many different levels of heading does HTML support?
fixed.w: HTML supports six heading levels, <h1> to <h6>.

fixed.q: The default character encoding in HTML5 is ____.
fixed.w: HTML5 defaults to UTF-8.

fixed.q: What does <main> include?
fixed.w: <main> holds the page's main content, such as <article>. Headers, footers and sidebars (<aside>) that repeat across pages go outside it.

fixed.q: Which of these is HTML code?
fixed.w: HTML code is made of elements, written with tags that carry attributes.

fixed.q: Which of the following tags is used to mark the beginning of a paragraph?
fixed.w: starts a paragraph.

fixed.q: Correct HTML tag for the largest heading is
fixed.w: <h1> is the largest heading.

fixed.q: Which of the following rule is needed to be followed while declaring the XML (Extensible Markup Language) elements name?
o: Name must not start with the letter xml
Name must start with a number
Name cannot contain letter, numbers and other characters
fixed.w: XML element names must not start with 'xml' (any case), cannot start with a digit or punctuation, and cannot contain spaces.

fixed.q: ______ reads XML documents and provides access to their content and structure.
fixed.w: An XML processor (parser) reads XML documents and gives applications access to their content and structure.

fixed.q:
What will the output of the following code snippet be?
<script> document.write("Hello") document.write("\\nIndia") </script>
fixed.w: In HTML, \\n is rendered as whitespace, so the page shows 'Hello India'.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a valid syntax for the XML element in a DTD?
fixed.w: A DTD declares an element as <!ELEMENT element-name category>.

fixed.q: Which of the following types of XML parsers is an object that contains all the information of an XML document and is composed like a tree structure?
fixed.w: A DOM parser builds an in-memory tree object of the whole XML document; SAX is event-driven.

fixed.q: Which of the following methods is used to slide down an element?
fixed.w: JQuery's slideDown() reveals an element with a sliding motion.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT an XML Parser?
fixed.w: DOM, SAX and JDOM are XML parsers; 'Shell' is not.

fixed.q: How to write the external DTD?
fixed.w: An external DTD is declared <!DOCTYPE root-element SYSTEM "file-name">.

fixed.q: Which directive is used for binding the model data to the view?
fixed.w: Ng-model binds input data to the model (two-way binding).

fixed.q:
Match the column JavaScript-Events with the column Descriptions.
Events: a) onchange; b) onmouseover; c) onkeydown; d) onload

Descriptions: i) The browser has finished loading the page; ii) An HTML element has been changed; iii) The user moves the mouse over an HTML element; iv) The user pushes a keyboard key.
fixed.w: Onchange = element changed (ii), onmouseover = mouse over (iii), onkeydown = key pressed (iv), onload = page loaded (i).

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) XML schemas define datatypes for elements and attributes, while DTD doesn't support datatypes. ii) DTDs are the declarations that define a document type for SGML. iii) In XML, tag names can begin with a numeric value.
fixed.w: XML Schema supports datatypes while a DTD doesn't, and DTDs come from SGML. XML names cannot start with a digit, so iii is false.

fixed.q: What is/are the purpose(s) of JavaScript events? i) Provide a dynamic interface to a webpage. ii) Provide a static interface to a webpage.
fixed.w: JavaScript events make a page dynamic and interactive.

fixed.q: Which of the following is used to comment out multiple lines in an XML file?
o: <!-- This is a multi-line XML comment -->
/* This XML file contains a list of custom information */
// This is a multi-line XML comment //
<-- This XML file contains a list of custom information -->
fixed.w: XML comments use <!-- … -->, which can span multiple lines.

fixed.q: In java script a ______ function can be defined as a function passed into another function as a parameter.
fixed.w: A callback is a function passed to another function as an argument and called later.

fixed.q: ______ is the standard that defines how web servers and application programs communicate.
fixed.w: CGI (Common Gateway Interface) is the standard for how a web server passes requests to application programs. The official key says HTTP, but HTTP is the browser–server protocol, not the server–program interface. (The official key was wrong here; this is the corrected answer.)

fixed.q: ______ are a database application's universal front end that connects to the back end via the internet.
fixed.w: Web browsers serve as the universal front end for web-based database applications.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a software application that helps developers to build attractive website layouts and apps with ease?
fixed.w: Front-end development tools help build website layouts and app interfaces.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a front-end design tool?
fixed.w: PHP is a server-side (back-end) language; Angular JS, jQuery and Chrome DevTools are front-end tools.

fixed.q: Which of the following can be used for the frontend or user interface while developing a web application?
fixed.w: JavaScript runs in the browser (front end); PHP, Django and SQL are back-end.

fixed.q: ______ is the process of visiting different websites on the internet hosted by various companies, organisations, educational institutions, magazines, individuals, etc.
fixed.w: Visiting websites is web surfing (browsing).

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a front-end technology?
fixed.w: PL/SQL is Oracle's database (back-end) language.

fixed.q:
Match LIST-I with LIST-II.
LIST-I: a) Front-End Framework; b) Front-End Asset; c) Front-End Boilerplate; d) JavaScript Library

LIST-II: i) React JS; ii) Tailwind CSS; iii) Font Awesome; iv) Reset CSS
fixed.w: Framework = Tailwind CSS, Asset = Font Awesome, Boilerplate = Reset CSS, JS library = React JS.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: A web browser is a program that can display a web page.
A web browser is a program used to view HTML documents.
A web browser enables a user to access resources on the Internet.
fixed.w: All three describe a browser.

fixed.q: Which of the following is not used to generate dynamic web pages?
fixed.w: PHP, ASP.NET and JSP are all server-side technologies for dynamic pages.

fixed.q: A ____ is a program running on a server machine that accepts requests from a web browser and sends back results in the form of HTML documents.
fixed.w: This is the definition of a web server.

fixed.q: Web links are stored within the page itself, and when you wish to 'jump' to the page that is linked, you select the hotspot or anchor. This technique is called
fixed.w: Text with embedded links you click to jump is hypertext.

fixed.q: Which one of the following is not used to generate dynamic web pages?
fixed.w: PHP, ASP.NET and JSP all generate dynamic pages, so 'none of these'.

fixed.q: With reference to CSS, which of the following allows to change property values smoothly over a given duration?
fixed.w: CSS transitions animate property changes smoothly over a set duration.

fixed.q: Which of the following front-end tools is one of the most widely used CSS extension languages across the world?
fixed.w: Sass is the most widely used CSS extension (pre-processor) language.

fixed.q: Which of the following is the syntax to write an external CSS?
fixed.w: External CSS is linked with <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="style.css">.

fixed.q: How to change all images to black and white (100% grey)?
fixed.w: The CSS rule is filter: grayscale(100%).

fixed.q: Which colour specification in CSS use three numbers representing the hue (from 0 to 360 degree), saturation percentage and lightness percentage?
fixed.w: HSL(hue 0–360°, saturation %, lightness %).

fixed.q: Adding the style attributes in HTML elements is known to be ____.
fixed.w: is an inline style. Internal styles go in a

fixed.q: The ____ CSS property allows a block of text to wrap around an image.
fixed.w: Floating an image (float: left/right) lets text flow around it.

fixed.q: If we don't want to allow a floating div to the left side of an element, the ____ CSS property will be used.
fixed.w: Clear: left stops floated elements from appearing on the left side.

fixed.q: Which HTML tag creates a hyperlink?
fixed.w: <a href="url"> makes a hyperlink. <link> (in <head>) attaches resources such as stylesheets.

fixed.q: Which attribute opens a link in a new tab or window?
fixed.w: target="_blank" opens a new browsing context. Other target values: _self (default), _parent, _top.

fixed.q: Which tag makes a numbered list?
fixed.w: <ol> = ordered (numbered) list, <ul> = unordered (bullets), <dl> = description list; <li> is each item.

fixed.q: Which attributes of <td> merge cells across columns and rows?
fixed.w: colspan="n" spans n columns; rowspan="n" spans n rows.

fixed.q: Which form method sends data in the URL query string?
fixed.w: GET appends name=value pairs to the URL (visible, length-limited, bookmarkable). POST sends data in the request body.

fixed.q: Which input type hides the characters typed?
fixed.w: type="password" masks the characters. type="hidden" is not shown at all and sends a fixed value.

fixed.q: Which of these is an empty (void) element in HTML?
fixed.w:
Void elements have no closing tag:
,
, , , , .

fixed.q: The alt attribute of gives:
o: Alternative text when the image cannot be shown
fixed.w: alt text is shown if the image fails to load and is read by screen readers. src gives the path.

fixed.q: Which is a semantic element introduced in HTML5?
fixed.w: HTML5 semantic tags: <header>, <nav>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer>. <font>, <center> and <frame> are obsolete.

fixed.q: Which HTML5 element is used to draw graphics with JavaScript?
fixed.w: <canvas> is a bitmap drawing surface controlled by JavaScript (getContext("2d")).

fixed.q: The correct HTML5 document type declaration is:
fixed.w: HTML5 uses the short <!DOCTYPE html>.

fixed.q: CSS stands for:
fixed.w: Cascading: when several rules apply, priority (specificity, order, !important) decides which wins.

fixed.q: Which CSS has the highest priority (without !important)?
fixed.w: Inline (style attribute) beats internal (<style>) and external (<link>) styles; !important overrides normal declarations.

fixed.q: In the CSS box model, the space between the content and the border is:
fixed.w: From inside out: content → padding → border → margin.

fixed.q: Which selector selects an element with id="top"?
fixed.w: # selects by id, . selects by class, * selects all elements.

fixed.q: Which CSS property changes text colour?
fixed.w: color sets the text colour; background-color sets the background.

fixed.q: position: absolute positions an element relative to its:
fixed.w: absolute: relative to the nearest ancestor with position other than static. fixed: relative to the viewport. relative: offset from its normal position.

fixed.q: display: none differs from visibility: hidden because display: none:
o: Removes the element from the layout
Keeps the space of the element
fixed.w: display: none removes the element and its space. visibility: hidden hides it but keeps its space.

fixed.q: In JavaScript, typeof null returns:
fixed.w: A long-standing quirk of JavaScript: typeof null is "object".

fixed.q: In JavaScript, 2 + "2" evaluates to:
fixed.w: With + and a string operand, JavaScript converts the number to a string and concatenates.

fixed.q: The JavaScript operator that compares both value and type is:
fixed.w: === is strict equality (no type conversion); == converts types before comparing, so 5 == "5" is true but 5 === "5" is false.

fixed.q: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
fixed.w: const: block-scoped, no reassignment. let: block-scoped, can be reassigned. var: function-scoped.

fixed.q: Which method selects an element by its id in the DOM?
fixed.w: getElementById returns the single element with that id.

fixed.q: An XML document that follows XML syntax rules is called:
fixed.w: Well-formed: correct syntax (one root, properly nested and closed tags). Valid: well-formed and also conforms to a DTD or XSD.

fixed.q: Which language transforms XML documents into other formats such as HTML?
fixed.w: XSLT transforms XML. XPath navigates nodes. DTD and XSD define structure.

fixed.q: HTTP status code 404 means:
fixed.w: 200 OK, 301 Moved Permanently, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error.

fixed.q: HTTP status codes in the 5xx range indicate:
fixed.w: 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client errors, 5xx server errors.

fixed.q: The default port of HTTPS is:
fixed.w: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, FTP 21, SSH 22, SMTP 25, DNS 53.

fixed.q: HTTP is called a stateless protocol because:
o: The server keeps no memory of earlier requests
fixed.w: Each HTTP request is independent; cookies and sessions are used to keep state.

fixed.q: A small piece of data stored by the browser and sent back to the server with each request is a:
fixed.w: Cookies are stored on the client. Session data is stored on the server and identified by a session ID, usually kept in a cookie.

fixed.q: Which of these is a server-side scripting language?
fixed.w: PHP runs on the web server and sends HTML to the browser. HTML and CSS are not programming languages; browser JavaScript is client-side.

fixed.q: The World Wide Web was invented by:
fixed.w: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW at CERN in 1989 (HTML, HTTP, URL). Vint Cerf co-designed TCP/IP.

fixed.q: DHTML is a combination of:
o: HTML, CSS, client-side scripting and the DOM
fixed.w: Dynamic HTML is not a separate language; it combines HTML, CSS, JavaScript and the DOM to change pages without reloading.

fixed.q: In Internet Explorer DHTML, "filters and transitions" were used to:
o: Apply visual effects (blur, glow, fades) to elements
fixed.w: IE-specific CSS filters (alpha, blur, glow, shadow) and transitions (blendTrans, revealTrans) gave visual effects.

fixed.q: The Tabular Data Control (TDC) is used for:
o: Binding data from a delimited text file to HTML elements
fixed.w: TDC is an ActiveX control; DATASRC and DATAFLD attributes bind table cells or fields to the data source.

fixed.q: In data binding with TDC, the HTML attribute that names the field to display is:
fixed.w: DATASRC points to the data source object (e.g. #mydata); DATAFLD names the column.

fixed.q: PWS, used to host websites on Windows 95/98 for testing, stands for:
fixed.w: Microsoft's Personal Web Server was a scaled-down server for publishing pages locally; IIS is the full server.

fixed.q: IIS is a web server from:
fixed.w: Internet Information Services runs on Windows Server and hosts ASP/ASP.NET applications.

fixed.q: In the DOM event model, an event that starts at the target and moves up to its ancestors is called:
fixed.w: Bubbling goes from the innermost element outward; capturing goes from the document down to the target.

fixed.q: Which is a rule of XHTML but not of HTML?
o: All tags must be closed and written in lowercase
fixed.w:
XHTML is HTML reformulated as XML: lowercase tags, closed elements (
), quoted attributes, proper nesting.

fixed.q: An XML parser that loads the whole document as a tree in memory is:
fixed.w: DOM builds a full tree (random access, more memory). SAX is event-based and sequential (little memory, read-only).

fixed.q: In a DTD, which declaration defines an element?
fixed.w: <!ELEMENT> declares elements, <!ATTLIST> attributes, <!ENTITY> entities. #PCDATA means parsed character data.

fixed.q: In a DTD, an attribute that must always be present is declared:
fixed.w: #REQUIRED must appear; #IMPLIED is optional; #FIXED has a constant value.

fixed.q: An XML document can be styled with CSS using the processing instruction:
fixed.w: The xml-stylesheet processing instruction links CSS (or XSLT) to an XML document.

fixed.q: An external DTD is referenced in the DOCTYPE using the keyword:
fixed.w: <!DOCTYPE note SYSTEM "note.dtd"> (or PUBLIC for a public identifier).

fixed.q: "Publishing" a website on IIS mainly means:
o: Placing files in a virtual directory/site configured on the server
Submitting the site to a search engine
fixed.w: The site's files go into the server's home or virtual directory (e.g. wwwroot) so clients can request them.

fixed.q: Adobe Dreamweaver and Microsoft FrontPage are examples of:
fixed.w: Front-end design tools let you design pages visually while generating HTML/CSS.

fixed.q: WYSIWYG stands for:
o: What You See Is What You Get
What You Save Is What You Get
Write Your Script In Your Web Graphics
Web Your Site In Your Way
fixed.w: WYSIWYG editors show the page as it will look while you edit.

theory.CSS:
• Cascading Style Sheets. Inline > internal (<style>) > external (<link>); !important overrides; more specific selector wins (id > class > element).
• Selectors: #id, .class, element, *, descendant (a b), child (a > b), :hover pseudo-class.
• Box model: content → padding → border → margin.
• position: static (default), relative (offset from normal place), absolute (nearest positioned ancestor), fixed (viewport), sticky.
• display: block, inline, inline-block, none (removes space), flex, grid. visibility: hidden keeps the space.
• color = text colour, background-color, font-family, font-size, text-align.
theory.XML & JavaScript:
• XML: user-defined tags, case-sensitive, exactly one root, all tags closed and properly nested. Well-formed = syntax OK; valid = also matches DTD/XSD. XSLT transforms, XPath navigates, DOM/SAX parse.
• JavaScript: client-side, dynamically typed. var (function scope), let and const (block scope).
• typeof null = "object"; 2 + "2" = "22"; "5" − 2 = 3; == converts types, === does not; NaN !== NaN.
• DOM: document.getElementById, querySelector, innerHTML; events: onclick, onload, onsubmit.
• Dialogs: alert, confirm, prompt.
theory.Internet & web basics:
• WWW: Tim Berners-Lee, CERN, 1989 (HTML, HTTP, URL). Mosaic was the first popular graphical browser.
• URL = protocol://domain:port/path?query#fragment.
• HTTP is stateless; cookies (client) and sessions (server) keep state. Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD.
• Status codes: 1xx info, 2xx success (200 OK), 3xx redirect (301), 4xx client (403, 404), 5xx server (500).
• Ports: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, FTP 20/21, SSH 22, Telnet 23, SMTP 25, DNS 53, POP3 110, IMAP 143.
• Server-side: PHP, ASP.NET, JSP, Node.js; CGI is the standard interface between a web server and programs. Client-side: JavaScript.
• Web servers: Apache, IIS, Nginx. Search engines crawl, index and rank pages.
theory.Internet programming (DHTML, XML, IIS):
• DHTML = HTML + CSS + JavaScript + DOM. IE filters (alpha, blur, glow, shadow) and transitions (blendTrans, revealTrans).
• Data binding: Tabular Data Control (ActiveX) reads delimited text; DATASRC = source object, DATAFLD = field.
• Event model: bubbling (target → ancestors), capturing (document → target); event object, cancelBubble.
• Servers: IIS (Microsoft), PWS (Personal Web Server for Win 9x), Apache. Publishing = placing files in the home/virtual directory (wwwroot).
• XHTML: XML rules (lowercase, closed tags, quoted attributes, nesting, one root).
• XML: DTD (<!ELEMENT>, <!ATTLIST> with #REQUIRED/#IMPLIED/#FIXED, <!ENTITY>, #PCDATA; internal or external via SYSTEM/PUBLIC); styling via <?xml-stylesheet?> with CSS or XSLT; parsers DOM (tree) vs SAX (events).
